content.title: About
content.content: Fried onion rings are slices of onion that are deep‑fried until golden and crispy. They have a strong onion aroma, a slightly sweet flavor, and a crunchy texture. Rings are commonly served as a snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onion rings originated in the United States in the early 20th century as popular street food.
While most rings are made from yellow onions, shallots or sweet onions are sometimes used for a milder taste.
The coating typically combines flour, starch and spices, giving the rings their characteristic golden hue.
In many countries they are served with barbecue, ranch, or garlic sauces.
They can also be baked for a less oily but still crunchy version.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Onions are rich in quercetin and sulfur compounds that act as antioxidants and support immune function.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Phytochemicals in onions may help lower cholesterol and improve blood vessel health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C contributes to immune defense and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Despite their sweet taste, onion rings contain little simple sugar.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories; those watching weight should limit portion size.

items.title: Onion allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onion.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing frying oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Potential stomach irritation
items.content: Fried onions can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a standalone snack, in burgers, sandwiches, or as a side to steak. Dip them in ketchup, mayo, ranch, barbecue, or garlic sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rings in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days to retain crispness. For longer storage, freeze them in a single layer and reheat quickly in the oven before serving.
